lawyer:
Mr. H. N. Nandi, Advocate ----- for the petitioner. 
Mrs. Joya Bhartacharjee Advocate ----- for the opposite party.
parties:
Mymensingh Arya Dharma Gnan Prodaini Sava
Vs.
Sree Rabindra Narayan Paul
full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit for eviction of monthly tenant Brajendra Chandra Paul, the predecessor-in-interest of the opposite party, before the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Mymensingh being S.C.C. Suit No. 3 of 1985, on the ground of default in payment of rent and subletting a portion of the suit premises to an outsider beyond the knowledge and without the prior written permission of the landlord. It has been alleged that the defendant has been a monthly tenant in the suit premises at a monthly rent of Tk. 40.00 only since 1962. In course of time, the defendant in a clandestine manner illegally inducted one Nirode Chandra Sarker as a subtenant in the suit premises beyond the knowledge of the landlord. It has been asserted that when the matter of subletting a portion of the suit premises to an outsider became known to the Secretary of the plaintiff, a meeting was convened on 16.8.85 to discuss and consider the matter along with other matters and this meeting was attended by defendant Brajendra Chandra Paul. In that meeting Brajendra expressed his regrets for sub-letting a portion of the suit premises and proposed to pay an enhanced rent for the premises in question. In that meeting the rent was fixed at Tk. 301.00 per month and an unanimous resolution of the Managing Committee was adopted on this question. This resolution Ext. 1 (ka) was duly signed by defendant Brajendra showing his acceptance of the new rent but the defendant did not pay any rent in province of the new agreement in spite of repeated demands by the landlord, as a result of which he became a defaulter in payment of rent. Thereafter by serving a notice upon the defendant under section 106 of the Transfer Property Act, the tenancy in question was duly determined. The plaintiff has filed the present suit for eviction of the defendant on the round of default in payment of rent and for by sub-letting a portion of the suit premises to an outsider beyond the knowledge and against the consent of the plaintiff. 

 3. Defendant Brajendra contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that he is not a defaulter. It has been alleged that defendant Brajendra paid Tk. 16,000.00 to the plaintiff for construction of the suit premises for accommodation of his family and that of his brother Dhirendra Chandra Paul. After half of the construction of the suit premises was complete. Dhirendra expressed his unwillingness to reside in the suit premises and dissociated himself from the contract. It has been alleged that it was then settled between the defendant and the Managing Committee of the plaintiff that out of Tk. 16.000.00 paid to the plaintiff for the purpose of constructing the suit premises, Tk. 40.00 per month would be deducted as monthly rent of the suit premises till it was fully adjusted. It was also stipulated between the parties that after the full adjustment of the aforesaid sum of Tk. 16,000.00 the rent of the suit premises would be raised to Tk. 80.00 per month. It has also been alleged that it was stipulated between the parties that the defendant would be at liberty to induct sub-lessee in the suit premises but, in fact, the defendant never inducted any sub-tenant therein. it has been contended by defendant Brajendra that he allowed Nirode Chandra Sarder to reside in a portion of the suit premises for sometime on compassionate grounds, without receiving any pecuniary consideration. It has been asserted that the defendant, in good faith, put his signature in a blank paper on the representation of Sontosh Kumar Ghosh as a representative of the plaintiff in the name of 2 meetings. The defence, denied to have agreed to pay rent at the rate of Tk. 301.00 per month since then. It has been asserted that the plaintiff filed the suit with false and frivolous allegations for making illegal gains. 

 7. Mr. H. N. Nandi, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner, submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge seriously erred in law in dismissing the suit without properly discussing and considering the material evidence on record and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that in the face of the clear evidence of sub-lessee Nirode Chandra Sarker deposing as P.W. 2 that he had been a sub-tenant under defendant Brojendra for 19 years on payment of rent to him and in view of the consistent evidence of other P.Ws. and virtual admission of the contesting defendant of subletting a portion of the suit premises without any prior written permission of the landlord, the learned senior Assistant Judge was manifestly wrong in not decreeing the suit on the ground of inducting sub-tenant in the suit premises and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate submits that even if the defence plea regarding adjustment of Tk. 16,000.00 against monthly rent is assumed to the correct, still then the entire amount was fully adjusted much before the pronouncement of the judgment and, in that view of the matter, the defendant must be adjudged as a defaulter in payment of rent in respect o the suit premises and as such the learned Senior Assistant Judge was manifestly wrong in not decreeing the suit on the ground of default in payment of rent. 

 11. Himangshu Jyoti Ray as the Secretary of the plaintiff Durgabari Arya Dharma Gnan Pradaini Sava deposed as P.W.1. He stated in his evidence that defendant Brajendra had been a tendant in the suit premises at a monthly rental of Tk. 40.00 since 1962. He stated that subsequently defendant Brajendra illegally inducted subtenant Nirode without the prior approval of the plaintiff. He went on to state that on query from Nirode, he came to learn that defendant Brojendra had injucted him in the suit premises at a monthly rental of Tk. 200.00. Thereafter defendant was called in a meeting of the Managing Committee of the plaintiff Dharma Sava on 16.6.83, where the defendant expressed his regrets for his misdeed and begged to be excused. In that meeting the rent of the suit premises was mutually settled at Tk. 301.00 per month and an unanimous resolution of the Managing Committee of the plaintiff was adopted and defendant Brajendra duly signed the said resolution signifying his acceptance of the new rent. The relevant resolution dated 16.6.83 has been marked as Ext. 1 and signature of defendant Brajendra therein has been marked as Ext. 1(ka). He further stated that since the defendant did not pay any rent to the plaintiff in spite of repeated demands, the plaintiff served a notice upon the defendant under section 106 of the Transfer Property Act Ext. 2 determining the tenancy. He admitted that the defendant had paid to the plaintiff Tk. 16,000.00 at the time of constructing the house. He denied that the defendant did not willingly sign Ext. 1 but his signature was obtained on a blank paper fraudulently. 

 In cross-examination he re-affirmed that defendant Brajendra of his own volition put his signature in the resolution dated 16.6.83 Ext. 1. He stated that although there was no specific agenda for enhancement of the rent of the suit premises, the matter was taken up under the miscellaneous head and resolution was duly adopted thereon. He refuted the defence suggestion that the defendant is not a defaulter and that he did not induct any sub-tenant in the suit premises. 

 12. P.W. 2 Nirode Chandra Sarker stated in his evidence that he had been a sub-tenant under Brajendra in respect of the suit premises. He stated that initially he paid rent @ Tk. 50.00 per month and subsequently it was raised to Tk. 200.00 per month. He further stated that later he came to learn that he was a sub-tenant under defendant Brojendra, who did not grant him any receipt against payment of rent. 

 In cross-examination he stated that Brajendra represented to him that he was not required to communicate with the plaintiff. He added that he used and occupied one room, one kitchen, one tube-well and a part of the suit premises. He further stated that for 3/4 years since 1970 he paid rent to Brajendra @ Tk. 50.00 per month and thereafter it was raised to Tk. 200.00 a month. He clearly stated in his evidence that he had been a sub-tenant under the defendant for 19 years. He refuted the defence suggestion that he was allowed to stay in the suit premises by defendant Brajendra for only 3/4 years on the ground of religious affinity. 

 13. P.W. 3 Jitendra Chandra Debnath, a member of the Executive Committee of the plaintiff, stated in his evidence that he was present in the meeting of the Managing Committee of the plaintiff held on 16.6.83. He stated that the defendant was present in that meeting. He also stated that in that meeting the question of sub-letting by the defendant came up for discussion and rent of the suit premises was re fixed at Tk. 301.00 per month and an unanimous resolution on that behalf was duly adopted. He put his signature in the resolution Ext. 1(ka). He clearly stated that defendant Brajendra also put his signature in the resolution agreeing to the new arrangement in respect of rent. 

 14. D.W.1 Rabindra Narayan Paul stated in his evidence that his father Brajendra and uncle Dhirendra had entered into an agreement with the Managing Committee of the plaintiff in 1962, following which they paid Tk. 3,000.00 to the plaintiff as a grant and they further paid Tk. 16,000.00 to the plaintiff for construction of the suit premises for accommodation of the two families. He stated that after half of the construction work was complete, his uncle Dhirendra from withdrew from the construct and demanded back his share of the money amounting to Tk. 8,000.00, which he had earlier paid to the plaint. Thereafter defendant Brajendra had alone to pay the entire money on the understanding that he would at liberty to induct sub-tenant in the suit premises as it suited his convenience. It was decided between the parties that Tk. 16,000.00 would be adjusted against rent @ Tk. 40.00 per month and after the said money was fully adjusted, the rent would be raised to Tk. 80.00 per month. He denied to have inducted any sub-tenant in the suit premises. He stated that his father Brajendra allowed his "গুরু ভাই" Nirode to stay in the suit premises for a few months on compassionate grounds. He denied that his father agreed to pay Tk. 301.00 as monthly rent for these suit premises. He further stated that his father Brajendra did not sign the so-called resolution dated 16.6.83. He stated that the signature of his father was fraudulently obtained on a blank paper in the name of holding a meeting. He stated that all there the papers relating to the suit premises had been lost. He went on to state that the money they had advanced was for construction of the suit house and it has not been fully adjusted as yet against rent lie asserted that they constructed pucca structures in the suit premises and as such they were not eject able tenants. He denied the suggestion that they are habitual defaulters and they have illegally inducted' sub-tenant in the suit premises. 

 15. D.W.2 Subodh Deb stated in his evidence that he knows the contending parties. He stated in his evidence that Nirode Babu was allowed to stay in the suit premises as a friend of defendant Brajendra and he was not a sub-lessee in the suit premises. He stated that the defendant has been residing in the suit premises since 1962 at a monthly rent to Tk. 40.00, which was to be adjusted against the advance made by the defendant. He stated that it was stipulated between the parties that after the full adjustment was made, the rent would be raised to Tk. 80.00 per month. 

 17. D.W. 4 Abdul Bari stated in his evidence that he knows the contending parting and he lives at a little distance from the suit premises. He stated that the plaintiff constructed the suit premises on receiving Tk. 16,000.00 from the father and uncle of D.W.1 Rabindra. He stated that the monthly rent was fixed at Tk. 80.00 out of which Tk. 40.00 would be adjusted against the advance made by the defendant. He stated that it was further stipulated between the parties that if the defendant incurred any expenses in respect of the suit premises, the same would also be adjusted against the advance. He further stated that Niroda was not a sub-tenant under defendant Brajendra. He stated that Nirode was allowed to stay in the suit premises by Brajendra as he happened to a disciple of a common preceptor. 

 19. This is all about the evidence on record. In this case certain things stand admitted. There is no dispute to the fact that the defendant has been a monthly tenant under the plaintiff since 1962. There is also no dispute to the fact that notice under section 106 of the Transfer Property Act was duly served upon the defendant, determining the tenancy. The case of the plaintiff is that, the defendant is a defaulter in payment of rent and he illegally inducted sub-tenant in the suit premises without the prior permission of the plaintiff. No written agreement-creating tenancy his been produced before the Court. It has, of course, been admitted by P.W.1 that the defendant has been a tenant in respect of the suit premises since 1962, which is not disputed by the contesting defendant. The receipt of Tk. 16,000.00 by the plaintiff is also an admitted fact. While the case of the plaintiff is that although defendant Brajendra was inducted the suit premises at a nominal rent of Tk. 40.00, subsequently the said rent was enhanced to Tk. 301.00 on the basis of a mutual agreement of the parties. The defence disputes this fact seriously. It has been alleged that the signature of Brajendra in the disputed resolution dated 16.6.83 showing acceptance of Tk. 301.00 as monthly rent by Brajendra was by way of is representation of facts. This resolution dated 16.6.83 adopted unanimously by the Managing Committee of the plaintiff has been marked exhibit 1. At least three of the P.Ws examined in the case were present at the time of passing the resolution. The signature of defendant Brajendra in the disputed resolution Ext. 1 showing his agreement to the new rent is an also an admitted fact. The contention of the defence is that this was obtained on misrepresentation of facts. In the facts of the case and the evidence on record, I do not find any cogent reason to hold that defendant Brajendra, a man of earthly prudence, put his signature on a blank piece of paper to be subsequently converted into a resolution. I find that rent was raised to Tk. 301.00 in the meeting of the Managing Committee held on 16.6.83 and defendant Brajendra was present in the meeting and put his signature in the resolution to that effect Ext.1 indicating his concurrence to the new rate of rent at Tk. 301.00 per month in place of Tk. 40.00 only fixed about two decades ago. Be that as it may, it is an admitted fact that the defendant did not pay any rent to the plaintiff at any point of time, except paying Tk. 16,000.00 as advance towards construction of the suit premises. The learned Senior Assistant Judge found in this impugned judgment that the defendant has been a tenant in respect of the suit premises since 1st January, 1962 and Tk. 11,080.00 was adjusted against monthly rent @ Tk. 40.00 till filing of the suit on 1.7.85 and there remains a balance of Tk. 4920.00 as unadjusted advance and as such the defendant cannot be found to be a defaulter. Even if the case of defendant is taken in its entirity, it is found that on the date of the judgment on 16.7.90 the defendant's arrear rent dues to the plaintiff comes to Tk. 6240.00 even @ Tk. 40.00 per month. In that view of the matter, the entire advance made by the contesting defendant was fully adjusted long ago, there being admittedly no further payment of rent by the defendant to the plaintiffs on any account whatsoever. 

 20. Section 10 of the East Pakistan Premises Rent Control Ordinance, which was in force when the disputed tenancy came into existence, prohibited any payment of advance for more than one month. The parties to the agreement appears to have acted against it and made an arrangement for adjustment of the monthly rent against the advance. Subsequently, Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 1963 and Premises Rent Control Act, 1991 (Act No. III of 1 991) made similar provisions. Section 10 of the present Act makes an agreement for advance payment of rent beyond one month void. If any advance beyond one month's rent is received by the landlord, the tenant is entitled under section 16 of an Act to make an application within 6 months to the Rent Controller and in that case the Rent Controller may order refund of the advance rent or adjust any sum so paid or deposited in any other manner. Be that as it may, in the facts of the case, it is difficult to conclude with any amount of certainty that the defendant was a defaulter in payment of rent on the day of institution of the suit, in view of the novel arrangement made by the parties regarding payment of rent. 

 21. Now the question that calls for determination by this Court is whether the plaintiff has been able to prove its allegation that the defendant illegally inducted sub-lessee in the suit premises without the prior approval in writing of the plaintiff. From the evidence on record, I find that induction of sub-lessee Nirode Ch. Sarkar in the suit premises by defendant Brajendra is virtually on admitted fact. The defence plea that Nirode was allowed to live in a portion of the suit premises for 3/4 years merely on humanitarian consideration has not been proved at all. On the other hand, it has been proved by the most consistent and corroborative evidence of competent witnesses that defendant Brajendra illegally sublet a portion of the suit premises to Nirode in a portion of the suit premises and realised monthly rent from him at varying rates. The evidence of PW.2 Nirode Chandra, a thoroughly independent and natural witness, fully corroborated by the three other PWs. and virtually admitted by the defence, unmistakably proves that defendant Brajendra inducted sub-tenant Nirode in a portion of the suit premises without the prior written permission of the landlord and realised rent from the said sub-tenant for years. The evidence of the D.Ws. on this point is widely discrepant and totally unconvincing. I, therefore, have no hesitation in finding that defendant Brajendra illegally inducted a sub-lessee in the suit premises without the prior written approval of the plaintiff and grossly violated the terms of the tenancy agreement and thereby rendered himself as an undesirable tenant, causing the plaintiff landlord serious prejudice. The defence plea that defendant Brajendra had an oral agreement with the plaintiff authorising him to induct sublessee in the suit premises but in fact, he did not do so but simply allowed Nirode to reside in the suit premises with the members of his family on gratis for a few years, is not only a contradictory stand but the same has also been disproved by convincing evidence on record. The defendant is thus found to have illegally inducted a sub-lessee in the suit premises in flagrant violation of the agreement for the tenancy and made himself liable to be adjudged as an undesirable tenant. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, I am of the firm view that the defendant offended the provision of section 17(1)(b) of erstwhile East Pakistan Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 1961 which was in operation at the time of creation of the disputed tenancy in 1962, by sub-letting a portion of the suit premises to an outsider without the prior written consent of the landlord. Similar provision has been made in section 18(1)(b) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 1963 and section 18(1)(b) of the Premises Rent Control Act, 1991. In any view of the matter, the defendant must be found to have grossly violated the tenancy agreement sub-letting a portion of the suit premises to strange for financial considerations against the consent of the plaintiff landlord and, indeed, made himself an undesirable tenant. It is unfortunate that the learned Assistant Judge failed to apply his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and the material evidence on record and fell in error in reaching his conclusions on a superficial view of law and fact. The approach of the learned Assistant Judge to this vital legal aspect of the case is depreciated. 

 24. While parting with the case records, I think it necessary to mention that a tenant is under a legal obligation pay rent regularly to the landlord and this alone can save him from ejectment. A tenant has no right to claim adjustment of any advance, that he might have made to the landlord, against monthly rent, as advance rent or any premium in any from is strictly prohibited by law. Such an agreement is void and consequently not conforceable. The remedy for the tenant in a case of advance is to move the Rent controller within 6 months of the creation of the tenancy for getting an order of refund or any adjustment as may be found just and proper. The tenant cannot avoid the mischief of ejectment in an action by the plaintiff on the plea that since he has made an advance to the landlord, he can not be adjudged as a defaulter for non-payment of rent till the advance was fully adjusted. I get instant support of this view in the case of Shamsuddin Ahmed Vs. Mohd. Hossain, reported in 31 DLR (AD) 155.
